lines.prompt: What is the maximum fanout of n1 now?

golden.reference: Depends on the team's buffer tree. Accepted values observed: 3 (Team3, 6.95, lost only the QoR fraction) and 16 (Team7, 6.96, lost only the QoR fraction). Original n1 fanout was exactly 690 (n1 is the reset input driving the RN pin of all 690 DFFs; verified in test72.v), so any correct post-buffering answer must be <= 16 and match the team's own output netlist.
golden.notes: n1 originally drives exactly 690 loads (690 .RN(n1) DFF connections in the original netlist), so after enforcing max fanout 16 its fanout depends on the buffer-tree topology. Score arithmetic from the reliable teams confirms team-dependent grading: Team3 (6.95) answered 3 and Team7 (6.96) answered 16, and both lost only the line-4 QoR fraction, so a fixed expected number would contradict one of them. Team4 (5.95 = QoR fraction + exactly one full line) matches accepted answers on every line except this one; it used the same 445-buffer scheme as Team3 (whose actual n1 fanout was 3) but answered 16 - likely the fanout cap rather than n1's actual fanout in its own netlist - and lost this line. Team2's log also answers 16, but Team2's exchanged log is a different run than its graded one, so its answer is only behavioral evidence and its score must not be used in reasoning. Checker: recompute fanout of net n1 in the team's written test72_out.v; claimed number must equal it and be <= 16.
